name: MonarchCodeBlock
title: CodeBlock
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Text with an androidx.compose.ui.text.AnnotatedString per line in androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll, androidx.compose.material3.FilterChip (wrap toggle), MonarchCopyButton
summary: A code sample with a header (title or language), copy, a wrap toggle, optional line numbers, light syntax colouring and a diff mode.
whenToUse: To show code people read or copy: an API request in settings, a configuration snippet in onboarding, a change in a message.
whenNotToUse: For a short token inside a sentence use MonarchInlineCodeStyle. For a single value to copy, such as a URL or key, use MonarchCopyField.
api: @Composable fun MonarchCodeBlock(code: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, language: String? = null, title: String? = null, diff: Boolean? = null, highlighted: Boolean = true, showLineNumbers: Boolean = false, showWrapToggle: Boolean = true, copyable: Boolean = true, wrapped: Boolean? = null, onWrappedChange: ((Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onCopy: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchCodeBlockLabels = MonarchCodeBlockLabels())

class MonarchCodeBlockLabels(copy: String? = null, copied: String? = null, copiedAnnouncement: String? = null, wrap: String? = null, added: String? = null, removed: String? = null, codeName: ((title: String?, language: String?) -> String)? = null)

options.name: code
options.description: The code, exactly as it is copied. Tabs are drawn as four spaces and copied as tabs.

options.name: language
options.description: A language id ("ts", "python", "bash", "diff"). Picks the highlighter and the header text. Highlighted: JavaScript and TypeScript, JSON, Python, shell, CSS and SCSS, HTML, XML and SVG, SQL, Go, Rust. Others are plain text, and an unknown id is shown as given.

options.name: title
options.description: Header text, such as a file name or what the snippet does. Also names the code. null shows the language name.

options.name: diff
options.description: Draws + and - lines as a diff. null means true when language is "diff" or "patch".

options.name: highlighted
options.description: Turns syntax colouring on or off.

options.name: showLineNumbers
options.description: Shows line numbers before the lines. TalkBack does not read them and they are not copied.

options.name: showWrapToggle
options.description: Shows the "Wrap lines" toggle in the header.

options.name: copyable
options.description: Shows the copy button in the header.

options.name: wrapped
options.description: Whether long lines wrap instead of scrolling sideways. null lets the block keep the state itself (saved across configuration changes), starting unwrapped.

options.name: onWrappedChange
options.description: Called with the new state when the user uses the wrap toggle.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Called with the copied code after each copy.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: copy, copied, copiedAnnouncement, wrap, added, removed and codeName.

options.name: headerActions
options.description: Extra controls in the header, before the wrap toggle and copy button.

states.name: unwrapped
states.description: Default. Each line stays on one line and the code scrolls sideways inside the block.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Long lines wrap inside the block; the wrap chip is selected.

states.name: diff
states.description: Added and removed lines get the diff fills and a visible + or − marker; hunk headers use the info strong color; file headers before the first hunk are muted and semibold.

states.name: copied
states.description: The copy button follows MonarchCopyButton: the system confirms on Android 13 and later, earlier versions show "Copied" for two seconds; TalkBack is told "Copied to clipboard" in both.

states.name: no header
states.description: With no title, no language, no wrap toggle and no copy button, the header is not drawn.

appearance: A subtle fill with a subtle border and medium corners; the header has the muted fill and its text in the muted text color. Code uses the code type role of the theme. Keywords use the info strong role, strings success strong, numbers warning strong, tags danger strong, attributes and properties AI strong, and comments the muted text color in italics; diff lines use the AI diff add and remove roles. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The tokenizer is ported from the web and gives the same tokens, without the web's incremental mode for streaming code. Kotlin names drop the iOS is/shows prefixes, as Material 3 does: diff, highlighted, showLineNumbers, showWrapToggle, copyable and wrapped (a nullable value with onWrappedChange in place of an optional Binding). labels.codeName receives the title and the language id, as the web label function does. The wrap toggle is a Material 3 FilterChip, the Android form of a text toggle (see toggle-button); the web uses a ghost button with aria-pressed. The web code region is focusable so a keyboard can scroll it; on Android it scrolls by touch and TalkBack reads it line by line. The web has a CodeTabs companion for one sample in several languages; on Android put several MonarchCodeBlock in Material 3 tabs. AiCodeBlock's Apply and Insert are not part of this component.
accessibility: The code region carries the name of the code as its content description: the title, else "<Language> code", else "Code"; it is a traversal group, so its lines are read in order after it.
Each line is one element read as its text; added and removed lines of a diff start with "Added:" or "Removed:"; lines with only white space are skipped.
Line numbers and diff markers are not read, and diff lines carry a visible + or − marker, so a change does not depend on color alone.
The wrap toggle is a Material 3 FilterChip named "Wrap lines", read as selected or not selected.
The copy button is MonarchCopyButton named "Copy" followed by the code's name; after a copy its state is "Copied to clipboard" in a polite live region.
The code reads left to right in right-to-left layouts; the header follows the layout direction.
The header wraps at large font sizes, so the title is never cut, and the toggle and copy button keep a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: A final line break does not add an empty line; Windows line breaks are treated as line breaks.
Tabs are drawn as four spaces; the copied code keeps its tabs.
Empty code draws one empty line.
An unknown language is plain text, and its id is shown as given in the header and in the name ("toml code").
Every line is composed (not lazily); keep samples to a screenful or two.
The highlighter is not a grammar: unusual code can be coloured imperfectly, never changed.

examples.title: A file
Line numbers and a wrap state held by the screen
examples.code:
MonarchCodeBlock(
    code = "export const client = createClient({ retries: 3, timeout: 2500, baseURL: \"https://api.example.com\" });",
    language = "ts",
    title = "client.ts",
    showLineNumbers = true,
    wrapped = wrapped,
    onWrappedChange = { wrapped = it },
)

examples.title: A diff
examples.code:
MonarchCodeBlock(
    code = "@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@\n-const port = 3000;\n+const port = 8080;\n app.listen(port);",
    language = "diff",
    title = "server.ts",
)
